batch_history.semantic_review: Compared mechanisms and outputs with all preceding IDs and equations and linked the closest existing method. QR is an orthogonal triangular decomposition, pivoted QR exposes numerical rank, and complete orthogonal factorization supplies a minimum-norm solution with a right orthogonal factor. The SVD solve extracts a solution from singular values and vectors, while bidiagonal reduction supplies the intermediate matrix. Reduction of a symmetric pencil uses a positive definite metric, while QZ handles regular general pencils. Rejected LQ as a transpose counterpart of QR and grouped blocked implementations and storage formats under their underlying methods.

batch_history.semantic_review: Compared the existing distribution, regression, inference and scoring records for overlapping mechanisms. The logistic law describes a continuous residual distribution, while logistic regression predicts a Bernoulli class probability. The central chi-square law supplies a reference distribution for statistics such as Breusch–Pagan. Excluded beta prime because rescaling F recovers it, Lomax because generalized Pareto already covers it, and log-logistic because it is the d=1 Burr XII case. Kept Student t as the residual-law family and omitted its Cauchy special case.

batch_history.semantic_review: Fixed-step full gradient descent has no adaptive moments. The existing L1 proximal record is a standalone map. ISTA composes it with iterative gradients, and FISTA evaluates gradients at an extrapolated point with a distinct convergence rate. Frank–Wolfe keeps iterates feasible by convex combinations of linear oracle solutions. Quadratic penalty continuation instead solves a sequence of unconstrained objectives with increasing infeasibility costs. Step-size schedules and restart settings were excluded as stand-alone entries.

batch_history.semantic_review: Beta is a continuous probability law, while the registered beta–Bernoulli entry maps prior parameters and counts to a posterior and the beta-binomial is discrete. Generalized normal changes the exponent in the log density and contains Laplace at fixed shape, so it links to the preserved narrower law. Skew-normal tilts a normal density by a CDF. Normal inverse Gaussian is a real-valued mixture law distinct from the positive inverse Gaussian duration model. Screened out gamma as scale-equivalent to chi-square with unrestricted degrees of freedom, uniform as a fixed-shape beta, and Gumbel as a GEV special case.

batch_history.semantic_review: Secant carries two iterates and approximates the derivative by a divided difference; Halley adds curvature to Newton and has cubic local convergence at simple roots under smoothness assumptions. Steffensen applies Aitken acceleration to two successive images of a fixed-point map from the same iterate. It can be expressed as a secant step on g−I with an internally generated second point, so the entry documents that relationship and uses its one-state accelerated fixed-point interface. Excluded simple changes to Newton initialization and stopping criteria.

batch_history.mathematical_checks: Compared the explicit formulas with SciPy on synthetic knots, including exact node recovery, cubic reproduction, natural endpoint curvature, monotone grid evaluation and PCHIP zero endpoint and secant handling.
batch_history.semantic_review: Barycentric interpolation evaluates one global polynomial. Natural splines solve a global second-derivative continuity system. PCHIP estimates knot derivatives locally to preserve interval monotonicity and does not generally have continuous second derivatives. The existing isotonic fit pools violations in noisy data, whereas PCHIP interpolates given knots exactly. Excluded Lagrange evaluation as an equivalent representation of the same interpolating polynomial.

batch_history.semantic_review: Fixed-step ODE methods advance a state using a specified differential equation. Gradient descent uses steps to minimize an objective, and the OU record gives an exact stochastic transition for one process. Forward Euler is explicit, while backward Euler and trapezoid solve distinct implicit equations and have different stiff limits. RK4 uses a fixed four-stage tableau, while RK23 supplies a paired local error estimator and stage reuse. Velocity Verlet splits the position and velocity updates and preserves Hamiltonian structure under its premises. Omitted separate records for leapfrog naming and step-size settings.

batch_history.mathematical_checks: Checked three independent shortest-path recurrences, negative-cycle detection, disconnected minimum forests and HITS singular-vector identities on synthetic graphs.
batch_history.semantic_review: Dijkstra finalizes nonnegative-cost labels in greedy order. Bellman–Ford relaxes by edge budget and detects reachable negative cycles. Floyd–Warshall runs dense dynamic programming by allowed intermediate vertices. Kruskal minimizes the cost of connecting every component and does not minimize source distances. HITS uses coupled singular vectors, unlike PageRank’s single damped random-walk score. Excluded heap choices and tie-breaking modes as entries.
